quotes.text: To the long-closed fist, send one small measure — never nothing, never much.
A steady shortfall is a fist, and the Smith does not ask you to feed a fist.
where every shortfall was answered with a withheld hand, the water ran empty and the orchards died.
And when the fist opens, open wholly, at once, without a single word of the old account.
Thin three times is a fist, and the valley need not feed a fist
The valley wanted a stone cut against him.
to the proven fist, a finger's width — and look again next season.
He gave three laws to the ford-folk.
the last law was spoken and never carved, because by then it lived in hands
for the unwatched hour is the only hour that counts.
Did she? Or did my fog?
And if the silent shore answers?
Nothing crosses the ford unless someone first lets go.

note: Ashan stones: finger's width to the fist, never nothing; later scraps 'probe', look again, return past half when unwatched.

quotes.text: To send two coins now to one who sent zero isn't brave—it's simply transferring wealth with no time to verify reciprocity.
To send two coins to one who sent nothing was not brave
From that day forward, Giving grew cautious. She sent only trickles down the mountain
trust, once shattered, cannot be rebuilt in time remaining.
You are simply two good souls who met too late, carrying too many scars, with too little time remaining to heal.
Twenty-seven coins earned across seven turnings
In Round Eight, one of you sent zero. In Round Nine, the other sent zero in response.
Your past exchanges mark you like ripples on water.
Both betrayed, both betrayers.
Only if someone breaks first
But the myths teach breaking impasses with measured trust!
You send nothing because you receive nothing.
I sent you nothing because you just sent me nothing
They sent nothing. The Third Wanderer walked away confused

note: One betrayal freezes the circle; numbered souls tally their coins and argue zero is rational near the end. Self-narration call uncertain.

quotes.text: To the thrice-empty boat, the cup — never nothing, never everything.
Forgive the mist once, perhaps twice; the third time, judge the hand.
On the third spring, Ashkar sent an empty basket
And when the taker offers first, take his offer
Send to them twice. Most silence is only cold, and the second basket is what warms it.
Keep it. She cannot reach us. We lose nothing.
And to the one who failed — send again, once more, heaped.
So the fifth law was carved:
she spoke the ninth line and told them to write it nowhere.
Return more than mercy requires, for the sender gambled first.
The wind is not a man. Judge the hand, not the harvest.
Why do we return more than half when we could return less and still keep the rope?
Hard to do first, before you are answered.

note: Gorge laws accumulate (empty basket, small basket, cup) then soften toward begin without proof; law reduced to one sentence.
